incidents.root_cause: Valid native-command STDERR was treated as PowerShell failure under Windows PowerShell 5.1.
incidents.prevention: Determine native command success from LASTEXITCODE; capture or redirect STDERR deliberately.

incidents.root_cause: Empty gh JSON output was not normalized before existence logic.
incidents.prevention: Normalize null/empty to an empty array and assert count before property use.

incidents.root_cause: A collection of commit objects was cast to Int32.
incidents.prevention: Use array cardinality with @(...).Count or a documented numeric field.

incidents.root_cause: Remote PR merge success was treated as proof that local main/HEAD was normalized.
incidents.prevention: Discover local state and perform only an explicitly authorized ff-only normalization when needed.

incidents.root_cause: CLI JSON decoded to a nested array shape that was counted incorrectly.
incidents.prevention: Flatten/enumerate the decoded structure explicitly and assert resulting cardinality.

incidents.root_cause: A native/tool error message did not terminate the mutation loop as assumed.
incidents.prevention: Use explicit exit-code gates and verify destination inventory after mutation.

incidents.root_cause: Placeholder values were issued inside executable commands.
incidents.prevention: Issue only real values or first discover and assign them programmatically.

incidents.root_cause: A multi-line script block was executed interactively without its complete variable context.
incidents.prevention: Deliver multi-line executable content as a file; console receives only invocation lines.

incidents.root_cause: Validation relied on presentation/form artifacts rather than semantic/content evidence.
incidents.prevention: Verify decoded content, hashes, semantic names and independently verifiable artifacts.

incidents.root_cause: A signing configuration flag was treated as proof of signing capability; identity scope also drifted.
incidents.prevention: Prove signing with a detached signature or throwaway-repo commit; keep project identity local.

incidents.root_cause: Windows path manipulation was applied to a server-relative URL.
incidents.prevention: Manipulate URLs as URL strings.

incidents.root_cause: CLI option behavior was assumed and a stale downloaded script was executed.
incidents.prevention: Read local help, capture CLI version, verify downloaded script identity/content marker before execution.

incidents.root_cause: A global clean-worktree precondition ignored exact expected recovery artifacts already materialized with verified bytes.
incidents.prevention: Classify worktree entries as EXPECTED or UNEXPECTED before treating non-clean state as unsafe.

incidents.root_cause: Non-ASCII punctuation embedded in a Windows PowerShell 5.1 script was decoded incorrectly and caused a parser failure before execution.
incidents.prevention: Use ASCII-only PowerShell 5.1 source by default; prohibit smart punctuation; use ASCII-safe markers or encoded payloads for Unicode document content; byte-check final script before issuance.

incidents.root_cause: Semantic content was matched using an exact multiline string whose newline representation differed between the document and Windows PowerShell source.
incidents.prevention: Normalize EOL or use bounded semantic parsing/regex before multiline matching; assert exactly one intended match before mutation.

incidents.root_cause: Controlled-document self-status and registry lifecycle/authority metadata were allowed to evolve independently without a mechanical coherence gate; document mutation also requires explicit canonical register rebind verification.
incidents.prevention: Normalize recognized lifecycle-bearing self-status values and compare them with document-register lifecycle state; fail closed on contradiction or ambiguity; verify source_commit:path and canonical SHA-256 binding after controlled-document mutation.

incidents.root_cause: Three related script-generation failures violated native-tool and dependency-order contracts: CLI stdout and stderr were merged before JSON parsing; a Windows PowerShell automatic variable name was reused as a function parameter and altered gh invocation semantics; and a remote merge commit was used for local Git graph validation before the object had been materialized locally. A fourth failure showed that a Windows PowerShell 5.1 script was issued without a mechanical parser gate, allowing ambiguous expandable-string variable interpolation next to a colon to survive generation and fail at parse time before execution.
incidents.prevention: Parse structured CLI JSON from stdout only while preserving stderr as diagnostics; treat PowerShell automatic/reserved runtime variable names as prohibited identifiers for script parameters and mutable state; distinguish remote ref visibility from local object availability and fetch/prove required objects before local graph validation; recovery remains discovery-first before repeating any authorized mutation. Require a zero-error Windows PowerShell 5.1 parser gate before issuance, and prohibit ambiguous expandable-string interpolation next to syntactically significant characters unless explicitly delimited or formatted.

incidents.root_cause: Two related failures occurred after SG-017 hardening: remote branch existence was treated as an error instead of state requiring classification, and simple git ls-remote output was wrapped in collection-return logic whose runtime shape was not proven, reintroducing scalar/array ambiguity.
incidents.prevention: Classify remote ref state before deciding an action; prefer minimal parsing of native output; explicitly prove function and native-command return shape and cardinality before indexing or property access; keep the parser gate as a necessary but not sufficient control.

incidents.root_cause: A coherence validator assumed generic claim_id and evidence_id fields instead of first binding to the observed governance schema. The active registers were schema_version 2.0.0 with canonical collections claims[] and evidence[] and canonical identifier field id. The assumption produced a false negative even though the governed claim and evidence objects existed.
incidents.prevention: Discover and bind schema version, canonical container, and canonical identifier field before object resolution; never infer equivalence from similar or legacy field names without explicit schema mapping; validate cross-register references bidirectionally and with exact cardinality to reduce both false negatives and false positives.

incidents.root_cause: A read-only runner used a PowerShell control-flow keyword in a value-expression position. The generated script was syntactically invalid for Windows PowerShell 5.1 and stopped before its intended adjudication.
incidents.prevention: Require the Windows PowerShell 5.1 mechanical parser gate before runner issuance; treat parser success as necessary but not sufficient; stop issuance when any parser error is present; preserve fail-closed anti-regression handling for documented failure classes.

incidents.root_cause: A TLS diagnostic runner waited on an asynchronous task through a wrapper that surfaced MethodInvocationException or AggregateException state instead of the underlying task fault. The wrapper state obscured the concrete transport exception and risked over-classifying the TLS root cause.
incidents.prevention: Distinguish timeout, cancellation, fault, and successful completion; unwrap wrapper or aggregate exception state to the underlying exception before assigning protocol or transport cause; preserve wrapper state only as diagnostic context.

incidents.root_cause: A minimal curl range probe treated curl exit code 63 from the configured max-filesize safety guard as proof that the resource request failed, even though the observed transaction included HTTP 200 and application/pdf metadata. Client safety-limit termination was conflated with server and resource response semantics.
incidents.prevention: Classify native exit status, HTTP response state, content metadata, persistence state, and safety-guard activation independently; never infer resource failure solely from a nonzero client exit code when stronger response evidence exists.

incidents.root_cause: A native-process helper reconstructed ProcessStartInfo.Arguments by joining an argument array with spaces. A logical git grep pattern containing whitespace was split into multiple native arguments, causing Git to interpret part of the intended pattern as another token.
incidents.prevention: Preserve native argument boundaries mechanically; do not rebuild an argument vector by naive whitespace joining when arguments can contain whitespace or escaping-sensitive content; use a proven quoting and escaping design or a verified argument-boundary mechanism.

incidents.root_cause: A read-only adjudicator referenced the ordinary variable ExactIncidentRegisterPresent under StrictMode even though no reachable initialization established that variable. The script parsed successfully but failed at runtime when the undefined variable was evaluated.
incidents.prevention: Initialize or mechanically prove every consumed variable on all reachable paths before use; retain StrictMode; do not treat parser success as proof of runtime variable validity; classify undefined-variable failures as runner defects unless independent project evidence demonstrates otherwise.

incidents.root_cause: A governed PowerShell runner attempted to defend optional property access with a null comparison performed after direct dereference. Under StrictMode, a missing property throws PropertyNotFoundException before the comparison can evaluate. The same design also directly dereferenced required properties without first mechanically proving schema presence.
incidents.prevention: Prove property existence through PSObject.Properties before dereference whenever presence is not already established by an exact validated schema. Treat direct property access followed by a null comparison as insufficient under StrictMode.

incidents.root_cause: A native-process helper continued constructing ProcessStartInfo.Arguments by joining argument strings while its guard rejected only space and tab. The guard therefore demonstrated only a restricted whitespace subset and did not prove preservation for quotes, backslashes, CR, LF, or other escaping-sensitive argument forms.
incidents.prevention: Do not describe a restricted argument guard as general boundary preservation. Either use a mechanically proven Windows quoting implementation or constrain the helper to an explicit safe-token alphabet that excludes every quoting and escaping-sensitive form used outside the proven subset.

incidents.root_cause: A line-normalization helper applied Trim() to git status --porcelain=v1 output even though the first two fixed columns encode index and worktree state. Trimming leading whitespace can collapse the semantic distinction between worktree-only and index-only modifications.
incidents.prevention: Preserve fixed-column native output exactly until its grammar has been parsed. Do not apply generic trimming to porcelain status records before interpreting the XY state columns.
